newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's Caldera turns 81, with gloomy presage.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's Caldera turns 81, with gloomy presage.

text.p: Venezuela's Rafael Caldera, Latin America's oldest president, turned 81 on Friday, facing growing labour unrest and an astrologer's prediction that he will be forced from office this year.

The grandfather of Venezuelan politics, with a career spanning more than 50 years, has seen his popularity plummet to record lows since he took office three years ago. Approval ratings are now at 20 percent, according to opinion polls.

With the country emerging from three years of unprecedented economic crisis, most Venezuelans appeared to blame their ageing leader for three-digit inflation, declining standards of living, decaying public infrastructure and rampant crime.
A month-long wave of strikes in the public sector over wage claims has threatened the government's economic reforms.
Now serving his second five-year presidential term, 20 years after the first, Caldera enjoys good health, according to his collaborators.
However, he has appeared increasingly stiff in recent weeks, sometimes looking lost and stuttering during public speeches.
"He certainly shows his age and doesn't look particularly nimble," one Western diplomat said.
Three months ago, an astrologer was briefly detained for predicting that Caldera would no longer be in power by June 8.
Jose Bernardo Gomez said Caldera's "most critical period ... will be between Feb. 5 and April 27, 1997."
